prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production animation extension of an ADOPTED pixel game character, not a redesign. The attached sheet is the approved design and poses at nearest 4x; use its first standing pose as exact identity, palette, scale and proportions. Same adopted deliberately ugly heavy sagging bullfrog, potato-starch gray-white/cream skin, tiny half-closed slit eyes, enormous drooping lower jaw and belly folds, stubby feet. Preserve exact design; NEVER big cute eyes or athletic slim frog. Body ~26 native pixels high, ~46 wide.
Create only these NEW motion poses: 3 columns x 2 rows, six isolated poses facing RIGHT. First four form a heavy low crawling/hopping cycle: (0) near forefoot planted forward, hind leg pushing, belly low; (1) forefeet bearing weight, far hind leg gathering; (2) far forefoot reaching, near hind gathering; (3) settle with opposite limbs. Keep mass and height, no high aerial leap or shrink. (4) short hit recoil with tiny eyes squeezed and jaw folds tightened, (5) recovering lowered posture. No tongue or soundwave in these poses; those are independent parts already supplied.
Transparent RGBA background, equal grid cells, generous transparent gutters, consistent full-body scale and ground baseline, complete feet and limbs. Clean chunky square pixel clusters for a small game sprite enlarged into the output, same muted palette, 1-pixel native dark brown contour, upper-left illumination. No smooth airbrushed illustration, no labels/grid/text/background/ground shadows/additional people. Same head and face in every cell. Meaningful limb changes, never just translated duplicates. Output only the motion sheet.
